459751.overview:
The aim of the game is to mine out gold nuggets.

Originally released on the ZX Spectrum 16k in 1983, this enhanced SAM Coupé version was written by the original author, Simon Goodwin, and released in 1993. It features a much greater colour palette and has an extra end game once all the deposits from the original mine have been extracted.

Playing Tips:
 
Include bends in your tunnels to limit the effects of floods and rock-falls. Be careful not to flood or block the lift-shaft.
 
All that glitters is not gold! Approach deposits carefully to minimise damage. Sometimes a rock-fall may break previously inpenetrable rock, allowing a new route.
 
Use existing tunnels whenever possible. The miner tires much more quickly when digging new shafts, especially if lots of gold is being carried.
 
Don't overload the lift. The safe maximum is 15 nuggets plus one miner - if you try to carry more you may fall to your death.

459858.overview:
The Garden Centre of the Universe is a strategy and management game released in 2011 for the SAM Coupé. The game offers a unique experience in a cosmic setting. Players navigate through various challenges, managing resources and making strategic decisions to progress. The game is played by competing against a robot to fulfill gardening quotas of increasing difficulty in a head to head battle

The game features two main modes: the Red Game and the Blue Game, each offering different scenarios and objectives. The visual style is simple yet effective, focusing on grid-based gameplay where players must carefully plan their moves. The storyline adds depth, inviting players to explore the universe's mysteries.

Use the joystick or QAOP to move and fire or M to perform actions. The action available will depend on which mode the player is in: walking/squishing, picking/planting or watering mode. The space bar is used to toggle between the three modes.

You begin with only 2 seeds to meet the quota but when a fully grown plant is left to photosynthesise freely it will slowly produce new plants in adjacent, empty squares. Picking a fully grown plant counts as one production unit and also puts a seed back in the basket.

It is only safe to carry 5 seeds at a time as they could react with the subatomic particles of dark matter also carried in the basket so this is the limit for all levels.

Planting on squares that contain cosmic daisies gives a growth boost to the new plant and your watering can contains heavy water to increase growth rates when needed. Occasionally small comets will fall providing some bonus D20!

When the quota is met a special seed will be available that can only be planted on your star square. This is a spaceship plant that when fully grown provides a one-way trip to the next level! Climb into your ship first to win. Fail to do so and it’s game over for you when the boss finds out…

459860.overview: A text and graphics adventure written in Colin Jordan's Sam Adventure System.

460045.overview: Port of the Game Boy version of Tetris to the SAM Coupé by Simon Cooke (Cookie of Entropy). Never actually released, but probably done some time around 1993-94. It was originally meant to be part of Entropy's ill-fated (but excessively advertised, well in advance) Statues of Ice Megademo, found behind one of the doors in the ice caverns.

460067.overview:
A quiz game, parodying the format of “Going For Gold”, a lunchtime TV quiz programme of the early nineties.

The questions are just recycled from Quizball, a much older Revelation Software game.
